# Basic mathematics

Math is the foundation of all quantitative methods.
And since this is about quantitative methods, it is natural that I start with foundation.
Many even want to skip this and only return notation and concept issues in later chapter. The dynamic nature/hyperlink means you can just click go to the math concepts.

It has become a standard materials for humorists about the uselessness of math (think about the use of sqrt of 25 or the use of a compas).
Mathphobia is real, and these jokes probably easy the trauma some people had about that in the past.
Confuse the difficulty and usefuleness.
They are almost uncorrelated.
Arithmetic opertion is easy and useful, proving fermat's last theorem is difficult but less usefull (in practice), partial differential equations are difficult and useful, and easy but less used.
The idea behind here is somehow easy and useful-applied
How do we reconcile that?
The goal is not to do PhD in mathematics or solve, it is having the tools we need.

As said above, most chapters are to support concept introduced later. We will end by recalling what is an exponential @sec-exponential, logarithm @sec-log, and end with difference @sec-difference and differential equation @sec-differential.
